fact: ARCEP Bénin states a bilateral protocol applying the ECOWAS regional roaming regulation was signed in Dakar on 12 December 2025 between Benin and Senegal (and between Togo and Senegal).

ARCEP Bénin, ARCEP Togo and ARTP Senegal officially launched free roaming between the three countries in Lomé on 24 April 2026; data in roaming fell from 10,000 to 2 FCFA per MB and call receipt is free for the first 30 days.
Tech Review Africa says the free roaming agreements were signed by Senegal's regulator head and his counterparts from Togo and Benin; no signing date is given, so the published date is used.
The free roaming arrangement between Senegal, Togo and Benin took effect on 24 April 2026 in Lomé, with free incoming calls for up to 30 consecutive days.
La Nation reports Benin's regulator took part in the 23rd general assembly of ARTAO, the West African telecom regulators' association, held in Lomé.
La Nation reports roaming accords were signed in Lomé on the margin of the ARTAO assembly between the telecom regulators of Senegal and Togo and of Senegal and Benin.
The regulators made the reduced-cost roaming system officially in force between Senegal and Benin, with free incoming calls for the first 30 days of a stay.

fact: On 2022-09-08 Benin's Minister of Digital Affairs and the Director General of the Smart Africa Alliance signed a memorandum (protocole d'accord) launching the Smart Africa Digital Academy (SADA) in Benin; the ministry calls Benin an active member of the Alliance.
The article of 2022-09-08 states that the first SADA training courses in Benin, on cybersecurity and artificial intelligence, had already started.

ARCEP Benin hosted a regional regulators' conference from 9 February 2026 with national counterparts from five countries and the regional regulator bodies EACO, ARTAC and ARTAO, under the EU-funded iPRIS programme.
